extracted.intended_audience: The Carpentries community — lesson authors, lesson developers, and potential volunteer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Pilot open peer review process for community-developed Carpentries lessons to determine eligibility for inclusion in The Carpentries Lab (and optionally for JOSE submission). The process defines eligibility, reviewer roles, review focus areas, and public GitHub-based review workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for submission to The Carpentries Lab
rubrics_metrics.description: Community-developed lessons are eligible for submission to The Carpentries Lab when they reach a state where they can be used by anyone familiar with The Carpentries teaching methods and sufficiently knowledgable on the lesson subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to lessons developed in The Carpentries Incubator. The Carpentries Lab collects lessons that have passed through peer review; example: 'Python for Atmosphere and Ocean Scientists' (reviewed and accepted at JOSE) is cited as the target standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of the lesson
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback from editors and reviewers will focus on the design of the lesson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design is a primary focus area of review intended to improve lesson quality; reviewers and editors provide constructive feedback aimed at making the lesson usable and pedagogically sound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of challenges as formative assessment tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback will focus on the value of its challenges as tools for formative assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate whether exercises/challenges meaningfully assess learners' progress and serve formative assessment purposes (i.e., help learners and instructors gauge understanding and guide instruction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of the content
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback will focus on the accessibility of the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will consider whether lesson content is accessible to intended learners (formatting, clarity, inclusive language, and barriers to access). The page does not enumerate specific accessibility standards but lists accessibility as an explicit review dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support provided to Instructors
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback will focus on the support provided to Instructors who wish to teach it in a workshop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess instructor-facing materials and supports (e.g., instructor notes, setup instructions, timings, facilitation guidance) that enable workshop delivery by those familiar with Carpentries teaching methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open/public review process (GitHub issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews will take place as publicly-visible issue threads on the GitHub repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review workflow is transparent and public (inspired by ROpenSci’s open peer review of software). Review comments and editorial decisions occur in visible GitHub issue threads rather than private channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process will be coordinated by members of The Carpentries Curriculum Team and reviewers will be members of The Carpentries community wherever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review assignments and coordination are managed by the Curriculum Team; reviewers are sought from the Carpentries community and JOSE also seeks volunteer reviewers (external volunteering link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary purpose of review: improve lesson quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary purpose of the peer review process will be to improve the quality of the lessons submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are formative and developmental, intended to help authors strengthen lessons and increase reusability, rather than solely gatekeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional JOSE submission after Lab review (paper requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors opt to also submit the lesson to JOSE, they will need to write a short paper to accompany the lesson; this will be reviewed at JOSE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing The Carpentries Lab review gives authors the option to submit to JOSE for journal publication and DOI assignment; JOSE has its own documented requirements (linked) that must be followed for journal acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted-lesson recognition and metadata requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To indicate to other community members that accepted lessons have undergone this process and met the standard expected, authors will receive a badge and banner for use in their lesson repository and pages respectively, a new URL under https://carpentries-lab.org/, and be listed in The Carpentries Lab community on Zenodo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the public signals and metadata/actions applied to lessons that have passed review; they do not describe evaluation criteria but are the acceptance outcomes and recognition mechanisms.
